groups.canonical_name: Competitive pricing pressure from Asian rivals
groups.definition: Emerging competitors, including state-supported Chinese semiconductor firms, may erode prices and market share.

groups.canonical_name: Critical materials supply and export controls
groups.definition: Key materials sourced from limited geographies face export controls and geopolitical restrictions that raise costs and lead times.
Cyclical and macro-driven swings in semiconductor end-market demand and capacity cause volatile orders, overcapacity, inventory buildup and price erosion.
High fixed manufacturing and structural costs mean volume declines or underutilization disproportionately reduce profitability.

groups.canonical_name: High leverage and debt service burden
groups.definition: Significant debt requires servicing and refinancing, diverting cash, restricting flexibility and potentially forcing asset sales or costlier financing.
Export controls, sanctions and trade barriers may restrict shipments to customers and access to markets or equipment.
Industry overcapacity, fixed labor costs and competitors' incentives force price matching that erodes margins.
Variable outsourced foundry pricing, rising in shortages, pressures gross margins.
Import tariffs and protectionist foreign policies raise costs and hurt competitiveness.

groups.canonical_name: US-China trade tensions hurting China demand
groups.definition: Trade tensions and weak Chinese economy reduce demand and margins in China.
Share price volatility may expose the company to securities class action litigation.
Long development-to-delivery cycles drive high inventory and volatile working capital needs.
